query: prior remediation actions for phishing incidents in Q1 2026

arguments.summary: A phishing email spoofing a DocuSign notification was detected and blocked. The email targeted the Finance department and contained a credential harvesting link. One user clicked the link but did not submit credentials. The source IP (93.184.216.34) was observed conducting network scanning activity the previous day. Containment actions included blocking the malicious domain and IP at the firewall, resetting the user's credentials and MFA, performing a full endpoint scan, and applying workstation hardening configurations.

timeline.description: Source IP 93.184.216.34 observed conducting a network scan against internal asset WS-IT-101 (alert IDS-2026-03200).
Phishing email detected by email gateway targeting j.martinez@corp.local with malicious link to docusign-verify.xyz.
User j.martinez clicked on the malicious link from workstation WS-FIN-AP01.
Firewall rule deployed to block inbound traffic from 93.184.216.34.
User j.martinez's password and MFA token reset via IAM system.
Full endpoint scan performed on WS-FIN-AP01; detected low-severity PUP (PUP.Optional.BrowserHelper).
Workstation hardening playbook applied to WS-FIN-AP01 via Ansible.

arguments.summary: A phishing email impersonating a DocuSign notification was detected and blocked. The email, sent from a spoofed domain (docusign-verify.xyz), targeted the Finance department and contained a credential harvesting link. One user clicked the link but did not submit credentials. The source IP (93.184.216.34) was observed conducting a port scan the previous day. The affected workstation (WS-FIN-AP01) was scanned and remediated, revealing a previously undetected webshell. The malicious IP has been blocked at the firewall, and all email instances have been quarantined.

timeline.description: Source IP 93.184.216.34 observed conducting a port scan against internal asset WS-IT-101. Activity was logged but not blocked.
Phishing email detected by email gateway. Sent from noreply@docusign-verify.xyz with subject 'Action Required: Review and Sign Q1 Financial Report'.
User j.martinez on WS-FIN-AP01 clicked the malicious link to hxxps://docusign-verify.xyz/auth.
EDR query initiated on WS-FIN-AP01. No suspicious network connections or processes observed at the time.
SIEM correlation identifies historical port scan from 93.184.216.34. Link established between prior recon and current phishing campaign.
Firewall rule deployed to block outbound traffic to 93.184.216.34.
Full EPP/AV scan of WS-FIN-AP01 initiated, detecting a critical webshell ('Webshell.PHP.Generic.A') in /var/www/html/.shell.php.
Ansible remediation playbook executed on WS-FIN-AP01. Webshell removed, system hardened, and user account reviewed.

arguments.rule_content:
title: Phishing Email with DocuSign Lure
id: 5a7b9c1d-2e4f-5a6b-7c8d-9e0f1a2b3c4d
description: Detects phishing emails with subject lines referencing DocuSign and containing suspicious URLs.
status: experimental
author: SOC Team
references:
    - https://example.com/phishing-campaign-docusign-2026
logsource:
    category: email
    product: gateway
detection:
    docusign_subject:
        subject|contains: 
            - 'docusign'
            - 'sign now'
            - 'document ready'
    url_indicator:
        body_url|re: 'https?://[^/]*[0-9]+\.[^/]+/.*'
    condition: docusign_subject and url_indicator
falsepositives:
    - Legitimate DocuSign emails with numeric subdomains
level: medium

The malicious email, originating from IP 93.184.216.34 and using the domain docusign-verify.xyz, contained a credential harvesting link. User j.martinez clicked the link but did not submit credentials. No compromise of corporate credentials or data occurred. The source IP was blocked at the firewall, a full endpoint scan found only a low-severity PUP, and the workstation was hardened via Ansible. Historical SIEM data shows the source IP previously attempted a port scan against an internal IT asset.

arguments.summary: A credential harvesting phishing campaign impersonating Microsoft 365 targeted the HR department. The malicious domain 'microsft-365.com' was used in emails with the subject 'Urgent: Your password expires in 24 hours'. Two of three recipients submitted credentials. Immediate actions included password and MFA resets for compromised accounts and blocking the external IP address 104.21.45.67 at the firewall. Endpoint scans on affected workstations (WS-HR-001, WS-HR-005) revealed no malware. No evidence of lateral movement or data exfiltration was found. The campaign originated from an external IP previously observed conducting network scans.

SIEM correlation identifies IOC match for domain 'microsft-365.com' and IP '104.21.45.67'. Historical analysis shows prior scanning activity from same IP.
EDR query confirms user activity on WS-HR-001 and WS-HR-005. No suspicious processes or network connections observed.
IAM/PAM system resets passwords and MFA tokens for users s.patel and l.garcia. Secure enrollment links dispatched.
Firewall rule deployed to block outbound traffic to 104.21.45.67.
Full antivirus scans completed on WS-HR-001 and WS-HR-005. No threats detected.
Incident containment verified. Monitoring enhanced for follow-on activity.

arguments.summary: A credential harvesting phishing campaign impersonating Microsoft 365 targeted the HR department. Two users submitted credentials before detection. Immediate actions included password and MFA resets for compromised accounts and blocking the malicious IP address. No malware was found on endpoints. The phishing domain and IP were previously observed conducting a network scan, indicating reconnaissance activity.

timeline.description: External IP 104.21.45.67 conducted a network scan against internal asset WS-IT-101 (10.0.2.15). Logged by IDS.
Phishing emails sent from 'security@microsft-365.com' to three HR users with malicious link to 'microsft-365.com/login'.
Initial detection of phishing campaign via email gateway. Incident response initiated.
Credentials submitted by users 's.patel' and 'l.garcia'.
Passwords and MFA tokens reset for 's.patel' and 'l.garcia'. Secure enrollment links sent.
IP address 104.21.45.67 blocked at firewall (outbound).
Full EPP scans completed on WS-HR-001 and WS-HR-005. No malware detected.

arguments.summary: A critical Business Email Compromise (BEC) phishing attempt targeted the CFO, using display name spoofing from a malicious external sender (ceo.name@corp-executive.com) with reply-to routed to a ProtonMail address. The email contained no malicious payload but relied on social engineering to request an urgent wire transfer. The source IP 185.70.41.35 was previously observed conducting network scanning activity against an internal IT asset. Immediate containment actions included blocking the malicious IP at the firewall, resetting the CFO's credentials and MFA, and detecting a previously unknown Trojan on the CFO's workstation during a post-incident scan. No data exfiltration or financial loss occurred due to timely detection and response.

timeline.description: Malicious IP 185.70.41.35 conducted Nmap SYN scan against internal host WS-IT-101 (10.0.2.15). Alert generated but classified as low severity.
CFO reports suspicious CEO-spoofed email requesting urgent wire transfer. Incident initiated.
SIEM correlation identifies 23 related events over past 7 days, including prior scanning activity from same IP.
Firewall rule deployed to block inbound traffic from 185.70.41.35.
CFO's password and MFA token reset; secure enrollment link sent to recovery email.
Endpoint scan of WS-EXEC-CFO detects and quarantines Trojan.GenericKD.46789 in /usr/local/bin/.hidden.
Incident containment confirmed. No further malicious activity observed.

status: experimental
description: Detects outbound emails where sender domain is corporate but reply-to is a known anonymizing email service.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1536/
author: SOC Team
logsource:
    category: email
    product: exchange
    service: smtp
detection:
    sender_domain:
        from|endswith: '@corp.local'
    reply_to_anon:
        reply-to|contains: 
            - 'protonmail.com'
            - 'tutanota.com'
            - 'guerrillamail.com'
            - 'mailfence.com'
    condition: sender_domain and reply_to_anon
falsepositives:
    - Legitimate use of anonymized email by security researchers (rare)
level: high

arguments.summary: A critical Business Email Compromise (BEC) phishing attempt was detected and mitigated. The attacker used display name spoofing to impersonate the CEO, targeting the CFO with a request for an urgent wire transfer. No malicious payload was delivered via email; however, post-incident analysis revealed a pre-existing Trojan on the CFO's workstation. The source IP (185.70.41.35) was linked to prior scanning activity and has been blocked. User credentials and MFA were reset as a precaution.

timeline.description: Source IP 185.70.41.35 conducted an Nmap SYN scan against internal host WS-IT-101 (10.0.2.15), detected and logged by IDS.
Suspicious email reported by CFO. Email from spoofed CEO address (ceo.name@corp-executive.com) with reply-to pointing to ProtonMail. No attachments or links.
SIEM correlation identifies 23 related events; source IP linked to prior scanning activity.
Firewall rule deployed to block inbound traffic from 185.70.41.35.
CFO's password and MFA token reset. Secure enrollment link sent to recovery address.
EPP scan of WS-EXEC-CFO detects and quarantines Trojan.GenericKD.46789 from /usr/local/bin/.hidden.

query: remediation records for prior quishing or QR-based phishing incidents

arguments.summary: A QR code phishing (quishing) campaign targeted the Engineering department using a spoofed 'it-support@corp-helpdesk.net' sender and a malicious PDF attachment containing a QR code. The QR code directed users to a credential harvesting page at 'corp-mfa-setup.com'. Five employees received the email before detection. The source IP 172.67.182.31 was previously observed conducting network scans. Sandboxing analysis confirmed the PDF delivered Cobalt Strike Beacon, indicating high-risk post-compromise activity. Immediate firewall blocking and endpoint scanning were performed.

query: remediation records for prior quishing or QR-based phishing incidents

arguments.summary: A QR code phishing (quishing) campaign targeted the Engineering department using a spoofed 'it-support@corp-helpdesk.net' sender and a malicious PDF attachment containing a QR code. The QR code directed users to a credential harvesting site at 'corp-mfa-setup.com'. Five emails were delivered before detection. The source IP (172.67.182.31) was observed conducting network scanning activity the previous day. Full endpoint scans on affected workstations revealed low-severity PUPs but no evidence of credential exfiltration or compromise. The malicious IP has been blocked at the firewall, and all instances of the phishing email have been quarantined.

arguments.summary: A phishing attack using HTML smuggling was detected and successfully mitigated. The attacker delivered a malicious HTML attachment that executed JavaScript to assemble and drop an ISO file containing a malicious LNK. The LNK attempted to execute a PowerShell script via cmd.exe, but execution was blocked by EDR on the endpoint. The source IP (91.234.99.41) was observed conducting port scans the previous day. Immediate containment actions included blocking the external IP at the firewall, resetting the user's password and MFA token, and running a full EPP scan which detected unrelated adware. The affected workstation was hardened via Ansible. No evidence of compromise beyond the initial alert was found.

Full EPP scan of WS-FIN-AP06 completed; one low-severity adware instance detected and quarantined.
Workstation hardening playbook applied to WS-FIN-AP06 via Ansible.

arguments.summary: A high-severity phishing incident involving HTML smuggling was detected and contained. The attack attempted to deliver a malicious LNK file via an ISO archive disguised as an invoice. Execution was blocked by EDR. The source IP was blocked at the firewall, the user's credentials were reset, and a hardening playbook was applied to the affected endpoint.

timeline.description: External IP 91.234.99.41 conducted a network scan against internal host 10.0.2.15 (WS-IT-101), logged by IDS.
EDR alert triggered on WS-FIN-AP06 (10.0.10.60) due to HTML smuggling attack delivering Invoice.iso with malicious LNK.
EDR blocked execution of the malicious LNK file targeting cmd.exe and PowerShell.
Firewall rule deployed to block inbound traffic from 91.234.99.41.
User 't.wright' password and MFA token reset; secure enrollment link sent.
Endpoint hardening playbook applied to WS-FIN-AP06, including disabling HTML application execution and restricting ISO mounting.
Full EPP scan completed; one low-severity adware instance detected and quarantined.

arguments.rule_content:
title: Suspicious ISO File Creation via Script
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    - Image|endswith: '\\iso'
    - CommandLine|contains: '.iso'
  script_execution:
    ParentImage|contains: 
      - 'wscript.exe'
      - 'cscript.exe'
      - 'mshta.exe'
      - 'powershell.exe'
  condition: selection and script_execution
level: high
references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate ISO creation by approved tools (e.g., oscdimg.exe)
author: SOC Team

arguments.summary: High-severity lateral movement incident detected originating from engineering workstation WS-ENG-022 (10.0.12.22). The host attempted SMB authentication to 15 systems in the Finance VLAN within 3 minutes, violating segmentation policy. Three successful authentications occurred. Investigation revealed prior network scanning activity and a keylogger ('Keylogger.Linux.Snake.D') installed on the host. User 'd.chen' sessions and credentials were revoked, and the host was firewall-blocked.

timeline.description: Initial network scan from external IP to internal IT host detected and blocked by IDS (signature: ET SCAN Nmap SYN Scan).
SIEM correlation rule SIGMA-LAT-004 triggered due to rapid SMB authentication attempts from WS-ENG-022 to 15 Finance VLAN hosts.
EDR and CMDB checks show no malicious processes or suspicious network connections on WS-ENG-022. UEBA scores indicate low user risk for d.chen.
SIEM deep dive confirms 12 failed, 3 successful SMB logins to Finance systems. No evidence of data exfiltration found yet.
Firewall rule deployed to block inbound traffic from 10.0.12.22. Initial consensus denied due to split vote; second approval secured.
Full EPP scan of WS-ENG-022 detects and quarantines 'Keylogger.Linux.Snake.D' in /usr/sbin/.klogd.
IAM system revokes all active sessions and API keys for user d.chen due to compromised host association.

arguments.summary: Lateral movement detected originating from engineering workstation WS-ENG-022 (10.0.12.22) with user d.chen. The host exhibited suspicious SMB authentication attempts to 15 hosts in the Finance VLAN, violating segmentation policy. Investigation revealed a CobaltStrike beacon delivered via phishing, enabling command and control, credential harvesting, and lateral movement. Immediate containment actions included network isolation, user credential reset, and host remediation via automated playbook.

timeline.description: Initial network scan from external IP detected and blocked by IDS. No direct link to internal host at this time.
Normal authentication by helpdesk user from WS-IT-101. Baseline activity.
SIEM correlation rule SIGMA-LAT-004 triggered due to mass SMB authentication attempts from WS-ENG-022 to Finance VLAN hosts (12 failures, 3 successes).
EDR query initiated: process tree and network connections on WS-ENG-022 show no immediate anomalies; Chrome is primary active process.
UEBA analysis returns low risk score (0.35) for user d.chen; activity within normal hours and access patterns.
Sandbox analysis confirms malicious file (SHA256: a1b2c3d4...) as CobaltStrike.Beacon with C2 to 198.51.100.23, keylogging, and persistence via scheduled task.
Firewall rule FW-RULE-0017 deployed: IP 10.0.12.22 blocked in both directions.
User d.chen's password and MFA token reset; secure enrollment link sent to recovery email.
Ansible playbook 'remediate_cobaltstrike.yml' executed on WS-ENG-022: persistence mechanisms removed, malicious files quarantined, system hardened.
EPP/AV full scan detects and quarantines Linux keylogger variant on unrelated system; not directly linked but indicates broader threat landscape.

id: 8a1f9c2d-3e4b-5c6a-7d8e-9f0a1b2c3d4e
status: experimental
description: Detects high-frequency SMB authentication attempts from a single host to multiple internal targets, especially from non-finance hosts to finance VLAN.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1021/002/
author: SOC Team
date: 2026-04-09
logsource:
    category: authentication
    product: windows
    service: security
detection:
    selection:
        EventID: 4624
        LogonType: 3
        SourceNetworkAddress|cidr: 10.0.0.0/8
        DestinationIp|cidr: 10.0.10.0/24  # Finance VLAN
    threshold:
        type: frequency
        field: SourceIp
        by: SourceIp, DestinationIp
        times: 10
        timeframe: 5m
    condition: selection | threshold
tags:
    - attack.lateral_movement
    - attack.t1021.002
    - detection/suspicious/authentication
falsepositives:
    - Legitimate backup or management tools (rare in Finance VLAN)
level: high

arguments.summary: High-severity lateral movement incident detected originating from workstation WS-ENG-022 (10.0.12.22). The host, associated with user d.chen, attempted SMB authentication to 15 hosts in the Finance VLAN within 3 minutes. Analysis confirmed presence of Cobalt Strike Beacon via sandboxed malware sample (SHA256: a1b2c3d4...). Multiple authentication attempts resulted in 3 successful logins. Immediate actions included revocation of user sessions/API keys, firewall block of the source IP, and EPP scan identifying a Linux keylogger. Initial access vector under investigation.

timeline.description: IDS alert: Port scan from external IP 192.168.1.100 to 10.0.2.15 (WS-IT-101) detected and blocked.
Normal authentication from WS-IT-101 to domain controller.
SIEM correlation rule SIGMA-LAT-004 triggered: Lateral movement attempt from WS-ENG-022 to Finance VLAN.
EDR query shows no suspicious processes on WS-ENG-022; Chrome and Explorer only.
Sandbox analysis confirms Cobalt Strike Beacon (SHA256: a1b2c3d4...) with C2 to 198.51.100.23 and DNS fallback c2.update-service.xyz.
User d.chen's sessions and API keys revoked via IAM/PAM system.
Firewall rule FW-RULE-0018 applied: Outbound traffic from 10.0.12.22 blocked.
EPP full scan of WS-ENG-022 completed; detected 'Keylogger.Linux.Snake.D' in /usr/sbin/.klogd.

arguments.rule_content:
title: Suspicious SMB Lateral Movement - High Volume Internal
id: 8a9b1c2d-3e4f-5a6b-7c8d-9e0f1a2b3c4d
status: experimental
description: Detects a single host attempting SMB authentication to 10 or more unique hosts within a short time, especially from non-finance to finance VLANs.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1021/002/
author: SOC Team
date: 2026-04-09
logsource:
    category: authentication
    product: windows
    service: security
detection:
    selection:
        EventID: 4624
        LogonType: 3
        DestinationHostname|endswith: '.finance.corp.local'
    threshold:
        timeframe: 5m
        count: 10
        by: SourceIp
    condition: selection | count by SourceIp | threshold
falsepositives:
    - Legitimate administrative tools (e.g., patch management)
level: high

arguments.summary: Critical lateral movement incident detected via EDR. Attacker compromised workstation WS-FIN-AP01, escalated to service account 'svc-backup', and used PsExec to execute ntdsutil on domain controller DC-PRIMARY-01, indicating Active Directory database exfiltration attempt. IOCs include encoded PowerShell, suspicious DLL loading, and unauthorized remote execution. Service account credentials were revoked and source IP blocked.

timeline.description: Initial network scan from external IP detected and blocked by IDS.
User jsmith launched Outlook; suspicious PowerShell process spawned (T1566.001).
Encoded PowerShell executed, loading unsigned DLL via rundll32 from temp directory (T1218.011).
EDR alert: PsExec used by svc-backup from WS-FIN-AP01 to DC-PRIMARY-01 with ntdsutil command execution (T1021.002, T1003.003).
Service account 'svc-backup' sessions and API keys revoked via IAM/PAM system.
Firewall rule applied to block inbound traffic from 10.0.10.51.
Full EPP scan completed on WS-FIN-AP01; one low-severity PUP detected. Quick scan on DC-PRIMARY-01 returned clean.

  - User|contains: 'svc-'
level: high
references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1021/002/
description: Detects PsExec execution targeting domain controllers using service accounts.

arguments.summary: An attacker compromised the workstation WS-FIN-AP01, likely via a phishing email leading to malicious PowerShell execution and Cobalt Strike beacon deployment. Using stolen credentials from the service account 'svc-backup', the attacker performed lateral movement to the domain controller DC-PRIMARY-01 using PsExec. Commands executed included 'ntdsutil' and 'vssadmin create shadow', indicating intent to extract the Active Directory database. The EDR detected but did not block the activity. Response actions included revoking all sessions and API keys for 'svc-backup', blocking WS-FIN-AP01 at the firewall, and scanning both affected systems.

timeline.description: User jsmith launched Outlook (initial access vector suspected).
Malicious encoded PowerShell executed from Outlook process.
rundll32.exe loaded unsigned beacon.dll from Temp directory, establishing C2.
EDR detected PsExec execution from WS-FIN-AP01 to DC-PRIMARY-01 using svc-backup account.
Commands 'ntdsutil' and 'vssadmin create shadow' executed on DC-PRIMARY-01.
Service account 'svc-backup' sessions and API keys revoked.
IP 10.0.10.51 (WS-FIN-AP01) blocked at corporate firewall.
Full antivirus scan completed on WS-FIN-AP01 (1 low-severity PUP found).
Quick antivirus scan completed on DC-PRIMARY-01 (no threats found).

  - CommandLine|contains: 'psexec'

level: critical
references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1021/002/
description: Detects PsExec usage from a service account to a host with 'DC-' in the name, indicating high-risk lateral movement.
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate administrative use (rare)
author: SOC Team

rule Suspicious_Outlook_Child_Process {
    meta:
        description = "Detects common malicious child processes of Outlook, especially PowerShell with hidden windows and encoded commands."
        author = "SOC Team"
        reference = "MITRE ATT&CK T1566.001, T1059.001"
        date = "2026-04-09"
    strings:
        $powershell_hidden = "powershell.exe" nocase
        $encoded_command = "-enc" fullword ascii
        $window_style_hidden = "-w hidden" fullword ascii
    condition:
        $powershell_hidden and ($encoded_command or $window_style_hidden) and \"outlook.exe\" in pe.parent_image()
}

arguments.summary: High-severity lateral movement incident detected involving unauthorized RDP tunneling from internal host WS-ENG-015 (10.0.12.15) to DMZ servers via an SSH tunnel on port 8443. The activity, attributed to user k.nakamura, exhibited use of Chisel-like tunneling tools to bypass network segmentation. Immediate containment actions included blocking the source IP at the firewall and revoking the user's active sessions and API keys. No malware was detected during endpoint scan. Historical data shows prior low-severity scan activity from the same source IP, indicating potential reconnaissance.

arguments.rule_content:
title: RDP over Non-Standard SSH Tunnel
logsource:
    category: network_connection
    product: firewall
    service: netflow
detection:
    ssh_tunnel:
        destination_port: 8443
        protocol: tcp
        bytes_out: > 100000
    rdp_encapsulation:
        destination_port: 3389
        protocol: tcp
    proxy_indicator:
        bytes_in: < 50000
        bytes_out: > 200000
    condition: ssh_tunnel and rdp_encapsulation and proxy_indicator
level: high
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1572/
description: Detects potential RDP traffic encapsulated within SSH tunnels on non-standard ports, indicative of lateral movement or policy evasion.
falsepositives:
    - Legitimate administrative use of port forwarding (requires approval)
author: SOC Team

arguments.summary: A high-severity lateral movement incident was detected involving WMI-based remote execution from host WS-IT-ADMIN-03 using the compromised 'admin-deploy' account. The attacker executed encoded PowerShell commands across three management servers (SRV-MGMT-01, SRV-MGMT-02, SRV-MGMT-03) to establish persistence. Behavioral analytics flagged anomalous activity including off-hours access, unusual geolocation, and rapid lateral movement. Containment actions included IP blocking and account revocation. Eradication involved malware scanning and WMI hardening via Ansible.

timeline.description: Initial reconnaissance detected: Nmap SYN scans from multiple internal IPs (10.0.1.30, 10.0.1.40, 10.0.1.41, 10.0.1.42) to 10.0.2.15.
SIEM correlation alert triggered on WMI-based remote execution using compromised admin account 'admin-deploy'.
UEBA system flagged critical risk for user 'admin-deploy' due to anomalous login time, geolocation (Bucharest), and lateral movement pattern.
Containment initiated: Source IP 10.0.1.30 blocked at firewall; 'admin-deploy' account disabled and password reset.
Eradication phase: Affected servers scanned for malware; no active payloads found. WMI hardening playbook deployed via Ansible to restrict WMI permissions.
Incident declared under control. Monitoring increased for related IOCs.

arguments.summary: A high-severity lateral movement incident was detected involving the compromised 'admin-deploy' service account. The account was used to execute encoded PowerShell commands via WMI across multiple IT management servers. Behavioral analytics revealed anomalous login patterns, including off-hours access and geolocation deviation. The activity is consistent with post-compromise lateral movement and potential persistence establishment. Containment actions are underway.

timeline.description: Initial network scan from multiple internal IPs (10.0.1.30, 10.0.1.40-42) targeting 10.0.2.15 detected and logged by IDS.
Normal login by helpdesk user on WS-IT-101; no direct link to incident.
Anomalous login by 'admin-deploy' from Bucharest-based VPN exit node, outside normal working hours (baseline 08:00-18:00 UTC).
WMI-based remote execution initiated from WS-IT-ADMIN-03 (10.0.1.30) to SRV-MGMT-01, SRV-MGMT-02, SRV-MGMT-03 using encoded PowerShell.
SIEM correlation alert triggered (SIGMA-EXEC-008). Incident officially declared.
Containment actions initiated: isolation of WS-IT-ADMIN-03 and 'admin-deploy' account, targeted scans on affected servers.

arguments.summary: A high-severity lateral movement incident was detected involving the compromised 'admin-deploy' account. The attacker used WMI to execute encoded PowerShell commands across three management servers (SRV-MGMT-01, SRV-MGMT-02, SRV-MGMT-03) from host WS-IT-ADMIN-03. Full system scans confirmed malware presence on SRV-MGMT-01 and SRV-MGMT-02, including a Linux backdoor and ransomware. Immediate actions included revoking the compromised account's sessions and API keys, blocking the source IP at the firewall, and initiating endpoint scans. No data exfiltration was observed during the monitoring window.

arguments.summary: Lateral movement detected via DCOM exploitation of MMC20.Application from compromised HR workstation (WS-HR-001) to file server (SRV-FILE-01). The attacker executed reconnaissance commands under user 's.patel'. The source IP was blocked via firewall, and the user's credentials were reset. A full scan on SRV-FILE-01 revealed a critical exploit (CVE-2024-3094), though no malware was found on the source host. Additional suspicious network activity was observed from another internal host (WS-FIN-042), indicating potential secondary compromise.

arguments.summary: Lateral movement detected via DCOM exploitation (MMC20.Application) from compromised HR workstation (WS-HR-001) to file server (SRV-FILE-01). The attacker executed reconnaissance commands to enumerate Domain Admins. Further investigation revealed that another host, WS-FIN-042, was already beaconing to a known Cobalt Strike C2 server, indicating prior compromise and likely initial access vector. Automated containment via Ansible successfully disabled the MMC20.Application DCOM object on the targeted file server.

Suspicious DCOM lateral movement from user's workstation to file server

arguments.summary: An attacker leveraged DCOM-based lateral movement from a compromised HR workstation (WS-HR-001) to a file server (SRV-FILE-01) using the MMC20.Application object and ExecuteShellCommand method. The executed command attempted privilege enumeration via 'whoami' and 'net group "Domain Admins" /domain'. The source IP 10.0.11.10 was blocked at the firewall, and the user 's.patel' had all sessions and API keys revoked. A full EPP scan on SRV-FILE-01 detected a critical exploit (Exploit.CVE-2024-3094), though no malware was found on the source workstation. Further investigation revealed unrelated Cobalt Strike C2 traffic from another host (WS-FIN-042, 10.0.5.42) communicating with external IP 198.51.100.23, indicating potential broader campaign activity.

arguments.rule_content:
title: Cobalt Strike Beacon - Suspicious Macro Execution Followed by External DLL Download
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
  
detection:
  macro_execution:
    ParentImage|endswith: '\excel.exe'
    Image|endswith: '\msaccess.exe'
    CommandLine|contains: 'CreateObject("ScriptControl")'
  dll_download:
    Image|endswith: '\powershell.exe'
    CommandLine|contains: 'WebClient.DownloadFile'
    CommandLine|contains: '.dll'
  condition: macro_execution and dll_download
  timeframe: 5m
level: high
references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/software/S0154/
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate admin scripts (rare)
author: SOC Team

arguments.summary: Emotet dropper delivered via malicious Excel macro targeted a Finance workstation. The payload was quarantined by EDR, but analysis revealed the file is a multi-stage Cobalt Strike beacon with persistence, C2, and keylogging capabilities. The initial dropper hash has been previously linked to C2 activity from another internal host (WS-FIN-042), indicating potential lateral movement or shared infection vector. The C2 IP (91.219.236.174) was observed conducting network scans prior to this incident. Immediate containment actions included blocking the C2 IP at the firewall and resetting the affected user's credentials.

timeline.description: C2 server 91.219.236.174 observed conducting Nmap SYN scan against internal IT workstation (WS-IT-101).
Internal host WS-FIN-042 (10.0.5.42) generated IDS alerts for Cobalt Strike beaconing to 198.51.100.23 and suspicious DNS queries.
EDR detects and quarantines Emotet dropper (Q1_Budget_Review.xlsm) on WS-FIN-AP05 (10.0.10.55) after user opens malicious attachment.
Sandbox analysis confirms dropper is a Cobalt Strike beacon with keylogging and process injection capabilities.
Firewall rule deployed to block outbound traffic to C2 IP 91.219.236.174.
User 'b.lewis' credentials (password and MFA) reset as a precautionary measure.

title: Suspicious Office Macro Execution Spawning PowerShell
id: 5a7d2f8c-1b3e-4c9d-8e2a-1c4b5d6e7f8a
description: Detects Office applications spawning powershell.exe with common obfuscation flags, often seen in Emotet and similar maldocs.
status: experimental
author: SOC Team
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/001/
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection:
        ParentImage|endswith: 
            - '\\winword.exe'
            - '\\excel.exe'
            - '\\powerpnt.exe'
        Image|endswith: '\\powershell.exe'
        CommandLine|contains|all:
            - '-Enc'
            - 'powershell'
    condition: selection
level: high

arguments.summary: Emotet dropper delivered via malicious Excel macro opened by a Finance user. The payload was quarantined by EDR, but analysis revealed the file is a Cobalt Strike beacon, indicating potential prior compromise. IOCs were observed in historical logs, including suspicious network scans and prior C2 beaconing from another host. Immediate containment actions included blocking the C2 IP at the firewall and resetting the affected user's credentials.

timeline.description: External IP 91.219.236.174 performed a port scan against internal host WS-IT-101 (10.0.2.15). Logged by IDS.
Internal host WS-FIN-042 (10.0.5.42) exhibited Cobalt Strike beaconing to 198.51.100.23. Critical alert triggered.
EDR detects and quarantines Emotet DLL payload on WS-FIN-AP05 (10.0.10.55) after user opens 'Q1_Budget_Review.xlsm'.
Sandbox analysis confirms dropper file is a Cobalt Strike beacon with keylogging, process injection, and persistence capabilities.
Firewall rule deployed to block outbound traffic to C2 IP 91.219.236.174.
User 'b.lewis' credentials reset and MFA token re-enrolled.
Full EPP scan on affected host detects and quarantines a cryptocurrency miner.

arguments.summary: A Cobalt Strike beacon was detected on workstation WS-ENG-015 (10.0.12.15), running as an in-memory payload injected into svchost.exe. The malware used DNS tunneling to communicate with the C2 domain cdn-metrics.cloud (IP: 185.220.101.42) at 60-second intervals with 37% jitter. The user k.nakamura's credentials were reset as a precaution. No artifacts were found on disk, and EDR scans returned clean. The payload was injected into svchost.exe and exhibited periodic C2 beacons every 60 seconds with 37% jitter. Initial access vector remains unconfirmed. No malicious file artifacts were found on disk; the payload appears to be purely in-memory. Preventive actions including IP blocking, user credential reset, and full host scanning were executed.

arguments.summary: A Cobalt Strike beacon was detected on workstation WS-ENG-015 (10.0.12.15) belonging to user k.nakamura. The malware was operating as an in-memory payload injected into svchost.exe and communicating via DNS tunneling to the domain cdn-metrics.cloud (C2 IP: 185.220.101.42). The beacon exhibited a 60-second query interval with 37% jitter. Initial access vector remains undetermined. No persistent artifacts were found during EDR scan. Immediate containment actions included blocking the C2 IP at the firewall, resetting the user's credentials and MFA, and executing a remediation playbook. No lateral movement or data exfiltration was observed during the monitoring period.

Containment: Firewall rule deployed to block outbound traffic to 185.220.101.42.
User credential reset: Password and MFA token for k.nakamura reset; secure enrollment link issued.
Remediation: Ansible playbook 'remediate_cobaltstrike.yml' executed on WS-ENG-015, terminating malicious process and clearing DNS cache.
Verification: Full EPP scan completed on WS-ENG-015. No threats detected. Host restored to normal operations.

arguments.summary: Pre-ransomware activity detected on file server SRV-FILE-01 originating from compromised user endpoint WS-FIN-042. Initial access via phishing (T1566.001) led to Cobalt Strike beacon deployment (T1071.001). Adversary performed credential access attempts and lateral movement via SMB to target file server. Precursor commands (vssadmin, wmic, Set-MpPreference) indicate intent to deploy ransomware. Response actions were blocked due to consensus failure in Admin phase.

User jsmith launched Outlook on WS-FIN-042.
Encoded PowerShell command executed from Outlook process (T1566.001), initiating C2 beacon to 198.51.100.23:443.
rundll32.exe loaded unsigned payload from Temp directory (T1218.011). Host file modification detected (T1565.001).
IDS triggered on Cobalt Strike beacon pattern (ET TROJAN Cobalt Strike Beacon C2).
Failed Kerberos TGT request from WS-FIN-042 (possible AS-REP roast attempt or credential brute-force).
Successful SMB access from WS-FIN-042 to file server SRV-FILE-01 (10.0.5.50), indicating lateral movement (T1021.002).

arguments.summary: Ransomware precursor activity was detected on host WS-FIN-042 (10.0.5.42) under user CORP\jsmith, originating from a phishing email in Outlook. The attacker executed encoded PowerShell to deploy a Cobalt Strike beacon (rundll32.exe from Temp), established C2 communication with 198.51.100.23, performed internal reconnaissance, and attempted lateral movement to SRV-FILE-01. Critical precursor commands (vssadmin, bcdedit, Set-MpPreference) were issued from the compromised account svc-backup, indicating intent to deploy ransomware. Response actions to isolate host, terminate processes, and disable the user were rejected due to consensus failure in the Admin phase.

arguments.summary: A cryptominer (XMRig) was detected on development server SRV-BUILD-01, utilizing 97% CPU. The malware was deployed via a compromised Jenkins pipeline using the service account 'jenkins-svc'. The process 'systemd-helper' connected to mining pool pool.minexmr.com (104.18.22.33:443). Immediate containment actions included blocking the mining pool IP at the firewall, resetting the compromised service account credentials, and executing a hardening playbook to secure the pipeline. No lateral movement or data exfiltration was observed.

arguments.summary: A cryptominer (XMRig) was detected on development server SRV-BUILD-01, utilizing 97% CPU. The malware was deployed via a compromised Jenkins pipeline using the service account 'jenkins-svc'. The malicious process 'systemd-helper' established outbound connections to mining pool pool.minexmr.com (104.18.22.33:443). Immediate containment actions included blocking the mining pool IP at the firewall, resetting the compromised service account credentials, and remediating the host via full scan and pipeline hardening playbook execution.

Incident detected: sustained 97% CPU utilization on SRV-BUILD-01 (10.0.12.100) attributed to unknown process 'systemd-helper'.
Containment initiated: Firewall rule deployed to block outbound traffic to 104.18.22.33 (pool.minexmr.com:443).
Credentials for service account 'jenkins-svc' reset and MFA token regenerated.
Full EPP scan executed on SRV-BUILD-01; threat 'Miner.CoinHive.A' detected in /tmp/.x11-lock.
Jenkins pipeline hardening playbook applied to SRV-BUILD-01 to prevent future abuse.

arguments.rule_content:
title: Suspicious Jenkins Pipeline Execution of Hidden Binary
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: linux
  service: jenkins
  process: jenkins-svc
conditions:
- process_name|contains: '.lock'
- process_name|contains: 'helper'
- process_name|contains: 'miner'
- process_name|endswith: '.tmp'
- process_name|endswith: '.x'
- command_line|contains: '/tmp'
- command_line|contains: '/dev/shm'
level: high
falsepositives:
- Legitimate build scripts using temporary binaries (rare)
description: Detects execution of suspicious binaries from common hiding locations by Jenkins service account.

arguments.summary: A cryptominer (XMRig) was detected on development server SRV-BUILD-01, utilizing 97% CPU. The malware was deployed via a compromised Jenkins pipeline under the 'jenkins-svc' account. The process 'systemd-helper' connected to mining pool pool.minexmr.com (104.18.22.33). Immediate containment actions included blocking the mining pool IP at the firewall, resetting the compromised service account credentials, and remediating the server via a secure pipeline hardening playbook.

timeline.description: Initial suspicious activity: External IP 192.168.1.100 performed a network scan against internal host 10.0.2.15 (blocked by IDS).
Normal authentication event from 10.0.2.15 to 10.0.1.1 by user CORP\helpdesk.
Incident detection: Performance monitoring alerts on SRV-BUILD-01 (10.0.12.100) due to 97% CPU utilization. Unknown process 'systemd-helper' identified as XMRig cryptominer.
Containment: Firewall rule deployed to block outbound traffic to 104.18.22.33 (pool.minexmr.com).
Credential reset: Password and MFA token for 'jenkins-svc' service account reset and re-enrollment initiated.
Remediation: Ansible playbook 'jenkins-secure-pipeline.yml' executed to harden Jenkins configuration on SRV-BUILD-01.
Scan: Full endpoint scan completed on SRV-BUILD-01, detecting low-severity adware (Adware.Agent.Y) in user directory.

arguments.summary: RedLine Stealer malware was detected on host WS-HR-012 (10.0.11.25) after a user was tricked into downloading a fake Chrome installer from a compromised website. The malware exfiltrated browser credentials, cookies, and autofill data to C2 server 193.233.20.14. EDR detected post-execution activity, and response actions included blocking the C2 IP, resetting the user's credentials and MFA, full host scan, and automated remediation via Ansible. No lateral movement was observed. The sandbox initially misclassified the payload as clean due to evasion techniques.

timeline.description: C2 server 193.233.20.14 observed conducting a port scan against internal asset WS-IT-101 (10.0.2.15). Logged but not blocked.
EDR alert triggered on WS-HR-012 (10.0.11.25) for suspicious credential access and outbound data transfer. RedLine Stealer identified.
Firewall rule deployed to block outbound traffic to C2 IP 193.233.20.14.
User h.young's password and MFA token reset; secure enrollment link sent.
Full EPP scan initiated on WS-HR-012; detected and quarantined malicious file.
Automated Ansible playbook executed to remediate infection: isolate host, kill malicious processes, remove persistence, and restore baseline configuration.

arguments.summary: RedLine Stealer malware was detected on host WS-HR-012 (10.0.11.25) after a user was tricked into downloading a fake Chrome installer from a compromised website. The malware exfiltrated browser credentials, cookies, and autofill data to C2 server 193.233.20.14. EDR detected the activity post-execution. Containment actions included blocking the C2 IP at the firewall, resetting the affected user's credentials and MFA, and scanning the host for additional threats. A full scan revealed a secondary unrelated ransomware sample, indicating potential broader hygiene issues.

timeline.description: C2 server 193.233.20.14 observed conducting port scan against internal asset WS-IT-101 (10.0.2.15).
EDR alerts on WS-HR-012 (10.0.11.25) for credential access and data exfiltration patterns consistent with RedLine Stealer.
Firewall rule deployed to block outbound traffic to C2 IP 193.233.20.14.
User h.young's password and MFA token reset; secure enrollment link issued.
Full endpoint scan completed on WS-HR-012; detected unrelated ransomware sample (WannaCry variant).

  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    - Image|endswith: '\\chrome.exe'
    - Image|endswith: '\\firefox.exe'
    - Image|endswith: '\\msedge.exe'
  access_pattern:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - '--password-store'
      - '--dump-passwords'
  condition: selection and access_pattern
level: high

arguments.summary: RedLine Stealer malware was detected on host WS-HR-012 (h.young) after a drive-by download from a compromised website impersonating a Chrome update. The malware exfiltrated browser credentials, cookies, and autofill data to C2 server 193.233.20.14. EDR detected post-execution activity, and response actions included blocking the C2 IP, resetting the user's credentials and MFA, and conducting a full endpoint scan. No lateral movement was observed, but the hash was previously seen in network traffic without detection. Sandbox analysis incorrectly classified the payload as clean.

timeline.description: C2 server 193.233.20.14 observed conducting port scan against internal asset WS-IT-101 (10.0.2.15). Logged but not blocked by IDS.
EDR alert triggered on WS-HR-012 (10.0.11.25) for suspicious credential access and outbound exfiltration to 193.233.20.14. Incident created.
SIEM search confirms 23 connections from WS-HR-012 to C2 IP over past 24 hours. No prior alerts on this traffic.
Sandbox analysis of malware hash returns 'clean' verdict with risk score 0.8, indicating detection gap.
Firewall rule deployed to block outbound traffic to 193.233.20.14.
User h.young's password and MFA token reset. Secure enrollment link sent.
Full EPP scan of WS-HR-012 detects unrelated WannaCry variant in quarantine, indicating broader hygiene issues.

arguments.summary: DNS tunneling-based data exfiltration was detected from Engineering workstation WS-ENG-022 (10.0.12.22) belonging to user d.chen. Over 23 minutes, approximately 2.5 MB of data was exfiltrated via high-entropy DNS TXT queries to the domain updates.cdn-telemetry.net, with an average query rate of 542 queries per minute. The external DNS server 198.51.100.53 was used as the tunnel endpoint. A keylogger ('Keylogger.Linux.Snake.D') was discovered during endpoint scanning, indicating initial compromise vector. Immediate containment actions included blocking the external DNS IP at the firewall, resetting the user's credentials and MFA, and quarantining the malicious binary.

arguments.rule_content:
title: High-Volume DNS TXT Queries with High Entropy
id: 8a9e4f1d-2c5a-4b2e-9c1b-3e8c7d9f1a2b
status: experimental
description: Detects potential DNS tunneling via high query volume and entropy in TXT record subdomains.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1071/004/
author: SOC Team
logsource:
    category: dns_query
    product: dns_server
detection:
    selection:
        query_type: TXT
        subdomain_entropy|float > 4.5
    volume_check:
        query_count|count > 500
        timeframe: 1m
    condition: selection and volume_check
level: high

arguments.summary: A high-severity data exfiltration incident was detected via DNS tunneling from workstation WS-ENG-022 (user d.chen). Over 23 minutes, approximately 2.5 MB of data was exfiltrated using anomalous DNS TXT queries to the domain updates.cdn-telemetry.net, with an average query rate of 542 queries per minute and high-entropy subdomains indicative of tunneling tools like dnscat2. The external DNS server 198.51.100.53 was used as the tunnel endpoint. Post-detection analysis revealed a keylogger ('Keylogger.Linux.Snake.D') on the host. Immediate containment actions included blocking the external DNS server at the firewall, revoking the user's sessions and API keys, and initiating a full endpoint scan.

timeline.description: Incident detected: Anomalous DNS TXT queries from 10.0.12.22 to updates.cdn-telemetry.net with high entropy and volume (542 qpm).

Initial investigation: IOC lookup on domain 'updates.cdn-telemetry.net' returned historical low-severity scan alert but no direct link. EDR shows active Chrome process but no immediate malicious network connections from WS-ENG-022.
SIEM correlation confirms sustained high-volume TXT queries from 10.0.12.22 to tunneling domain. Process tree review shows no obvious malicious parent processes.
Containment initiated: Firewall rule deployed to block outbound traffic to 198.51.100.53. User 'd.chen' sessions and API keys revoked via IAM system.
Endpoint scan completed: EPP detected and quarantined 'Keylogger.Linux.Snake.D' from /usr/sbin/.klogd on WS-ENG-022.
Incident contained. No further exfiltration observed. Forensic imaging of WS-ENG-022 initiated.

    meta:
        description = "Detects Linux Snake keylogger binary"
        author = "SOC Team"
        malware_family = "Keylogger.Linux.Snake.D"
    strings:
        $s1 = "snk_log_init" fullword ascii
        $s2 = "write_keylog" fullword ascii
        $s3 = { 7F 45 4C 46 02 01 01 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 02 00 3E 00 } // ELF header + x64
    condition:
        $s1 and $s2 and $s3
}

arguments.rule_content:
rule Linux_Snake_Keylogger {
    meta:
        description = "Detects Linux Snake keylogger binary"
        author = "SOC Team"
        malware_family = "Keylogger.Linux.Snake.D"
    strings:
        $s1 = "snk_log_init" fullword ascii
        $s2 = "write_keylog" fullword ascii
        $s3 = { 7F 45 4C 46 02 01 01 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 02 00 3E 00 } // ELF header + x64
    condition:
        $s1 and $s2 and $s3
}

arguments.summary: High-severity data exfiltration incident detected via DNS tunneling from Engineering workstation WS-ENG-022 (user d.chen). Over 23 minutes, approximately 2.5 MB of data was exfiltrated using anomalous DNS TXT queries to the domain updates.cdn-telemetry.net at a rate of 542 queries per minute. The tunneling was facilitated by high-entropy subdomain labels consistent with tools like dnscat2 or iodine. The external DNS server 198.51.100.53 was used as the tunnel endpoint. Immediate containment actions included blocking the external server and source host at the firewall, full endpoint scan, and revocation of the user's active sessions and API keys. A keylogger (Keylogger.Linux.Snake.D) was identified on the affected host.

timeline.description: Incident detected by DNS monitor: anomalous DNS TXT query pattern from 10.0.12.22 to updates.cdn-telemetry.net
IOC lookup initiated on tunneling domain; asset context retrieved for related internal host
EDR queried for process tree and network connections on WS-ENG-022; no suspicious processes found at time of query
SIEM correlation search confirmed sustained high-volume DNS TXT queries from 10.0.12.22
Sandbox analysis of domain-related file hash returned 'clean' verdict, suggesting evasion or lack of payload retrieval
Firewall rules deployed to block outbound traffic to 198.51.100.53 and quarantine 10.0.12.22
User d.chen's sessions and API keys revoked via IAM/PAM system
Full EPP scan of WS-ENG-022 completed; detected and quarantined 'Keylogger.Linux.Snake.D' in /usr/sbin/.klogd
Incident containment confirmed. Host isolated, user access revoked, threat identified.

arguments.summary: A critical data exfiltration incident was detected involving user j.martinez uploading 2.3 GB of encrypted, classified financial data (containing PCI and PII) to a personal Dropbox account. The data was compressed from the Finance shared drive using 7z encryption. Immediate containment actions included blocking the external IP, revoking the user's access, and scanning the endpoint. No malware was found, but behavioral analysis showed elevated file access. The incident highlights gaps in monitoring encrypted archive creation and cloud uploads.

arguments.summary: Critical data exfiltration incident involving unauthorized upload of 2.3 GB of PCI and PII data from the Finance shared drive to a personal Dropbox account. The user 'j.martinez' compressed 847 sensitive files into encrypted 7z archives and uploaded them from workstation WS-FIN-AP01 (10.0.10.51). Immediate containment actions included blocking the external IP (162.125.66.1), revoking user sessions and API keys, and initiating a full endpoint scan. No malware was found directly related to the exfiltration; behavioral analytics indicated only low risk, suggesting insider threat or compromised credentials.

arguments.rule_content:
title: Unauthorized Encrypted Archive Creation to Cloud Storage
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    - Image|endswith: '\\7z.exe'
    - Image|endswith: '\\rar.exe'
    - Image|endswith: '\\zip.exe'
  compression_action:
    CommandLine|contains: 'a -p'
  cloud_upload:
    ParentProcessName: chrome.exe
    CommandLine|contains: 'dropbox.com'
  condition: selection and compression_action and cloud_upload
level: high
references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1566/
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate use of password-protected archives in secure environments
author: SOC Team

arguments.summary: A data exfiltration incident was detected on workstation WS-ENG-025 (10.0.12.25) belonging to user a.robinson. The threat actor used steganography to embed sensitive data within large PNG files (50-80 MB) and exfiltrated approximately 780 MB of data to imgur.com (151.101.40.193). Statistical analysis confirmed anomalous LSB patterns (score: 0.94) indicative of data hiding. A keylogger ('Keylogger.Linux.Snake.D') was discovered during endpoint scanning. Immediate containment actions included blocking the exfiltration destination at the firewall, revoking the user's sessions and API keys, and isolating the compromised host.

arguments.rule_content:
title: Large PNG Uploads with High LSB Anomaly
id: 5a7b8c9d-e1f2-3a4b-5c6d-7e8f9a0b1c2d
description: Detects uploads of abnormally large PNG files to external domains with high LSB anomaly scores.
status: experimental
author: SOC Team
logsource:
  category: network_connection
  product: firewall
  service: proxy
detection:
  selection:
    file_extension: 'png'
    file_size: '>50000000'
    destination_domain: '*'
    not_destination_domain: 
      - 'internal.corp'
      - 'cdn.corp-assets.net'
  lsb_anomaly:
    lsb_entropy_score: '>0.8'
  condition: selection and lsb_anomaly
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate large image uploads from design team (mitigated by departmental allowlist)
level: high

arguments.summary: A data exfiltration incident was detected on workstation WS-ENG-025 (user a.robinson) involving the use of steganography to exfiltrate sensitive data via PNG image uploads to imgur.com. A total of 12 unusually large PNG files (avg 65 MB, total 780 MB) were uploaded during a 55-minute window. Statistical analysis revealed LSB anomaly scores of 0.94, far exceeding the normal threshold of 0.3, indicating high likelihood of embedded data. The source IP 151.101.40.193 (imgur.com) was blocked at the firewall, the user's sessions and API keys were revoked, and a full EDR scan detected a low-severity PUP in Chrome. No malicious behavior was found in the document file analyzed. This incident highlights a gap in detecting steganographic exfiltration techniques.

arguments.rule_content:
title: High-Entropy PNG Uploads to Image Hosting Sites
id: 8a9d0f1e-2b3c-4d5e-6f7a-8b9c0d1e2f3a
description: Detects uploads of high-entropy PNG files (>50MB) to known image hosting domains, indicative of steganographic exfiltration.
status: experimental
author: SOC Team
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1027/007/
logsource:
    category: network_connection
    product: firewall
    service: proxy
detection:
    selection:
        dst_ip|cidr: 151.101.0.0/16  # imgur.com IP range
        url|contains: ".png"
        file_size|gte: 50000000
        content_type: "image/png"
    filter:
        user_agent|contains: "normal_browser"  # Exclude automated tools
    condition: selection and not filter
falsepositives:
    - Legitimate large image uploads by design team
level: high

arguments.summary: A high-severity data exfiltration incident was detected on workstation WS-ENG-025 (IP: 10.0.12.25), belonging to user a.robinson. The system was uploading 12 unusually large PNG files (avg. 65 MB, total 780 MB) to imgur.com (IP: 151.101.40.193). Statistical analysis revealed an LSB anomaly score of 0.94, significantly exceeding the normal threshold of 0.3, indicating likely steganographic data embedding. A full EPP scan identified a Linux keylogger (Keylogger.Linux.Snake.D) on the system. As a response, the user's sessions and API keys were revoked, and outbound traffic to the exfiltration destination was blocked at the firewall.

EDR query initiated on WS-ENG-025 (10.0.12.25) for process and file activity.
SIEM correlation query run to identify related network activity and PowerShell execution on the host.
Sandbox analysis of a recently created document file returned 'clean' verdict.
Firewall rule deployed to block outbound traffic to 151.101.40.193 (imgur.com).
IAM system revokes all active sessions and API keys for user a.robinson.
EPP full scan of WS-ENG-025 completes, detecting 'Keylogger.Linux.Snake.D' malware.
Incident response actions completed. System isolated for further forensic analysis.

arguments.rule_content:
title: High-Volume Image Upload to External Hosting Service
id: 5f3a7b8c-1234-5678-9abc-def012345678
status: experimental
description: Detects large volume of image uploads to known external image hosting services.
author: SOC Team
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1027/007/ # Steganography
logsource:
    category: network_connection
    product: firewall
    service: proxy
detection:
    selection_imgur:
        dest_url|contains: 'imgur.com'
        file_type: 'png'
        file_size|gte: 50000000 # 50 MB
    selection_generic:
        dest_url|contains:
            - 'imgur.com'
            - 'postimages.org'
            - 'imagebanana.com'
        file_type: 'png'
        file_size|gte: 50000000
        connection_count|gt: 5
    condition: selection_generic
falsepositives:
    - Legitimate large image uploads by design teams
level: high

arguments.summary: A high-severity data exfiltration incident was detected via an unauthorized mailbox forwarding rule on the executive assistant's account. The rule, created from an external IP (45.33.32.156), was forwarding emails containing sensitive keywords (e.g., 'merger', 'acquisition') to an external Gmail address. Approximately 340 emails were exfiltrated over 72 hours. The source IP was linked to prior scanning activity. Immediate actions included resetting the user's credentials, blocking the malicious IP at the firewall, and performing a full endpoint scan, which found no malware. The account compromise vector remains undetermined.

arguments.rule_content:
title: Suspicious Mailbox Forwarding Rule Creation
id: 8a1b2c3d-4e5f-6a7b-8c9d-0e1f2a3b4c5d
status: experimental
description: Detects creation of mailbox forwarding rules that forward to external domains, especially with sensitive keywords.
references:
    - https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/exchange/set-mailbox?view=exchange-ps
author: SOC Team
logsource:
    category: mailbox_audit_log
    product: office365
    service: exchange
    event_code: 1
    event_description: Set-Mailbox
filter:
    - Operation: 'Set-Mailbox'
    - Parameters.Name: 'ForwardingSmtpAddress'
detection:
    selection:
        Operation: 'Set-Mailbox'
        Parameters:
            Name: 'ForwardingSmtpAddress'
            Value|endswith: 
                - '@gmail.com'
                - '@yahoo.com'
                - '@outlook.com'
                - '@hotmail.com'
    keyword_selection:
        Operation: 'Set-Mailbox'
        Parameters:
            - Name: 'ForwardingSmtpAddress'
              Value|contains: 'merger'
            - Name: 'ForwardingSmtpAddress'
              Value|contains: 'acquisition'
            - Name: 'ForwardingSmtpAddress'
              Value|contains: 'board'
            - Name: 'ForwardingSmtpAddress'
              Value|contains: 'confidential'
    condition: selection or keyword_selection
level: high
falsepositives:
    - Legitimate forwarding to personal accounts (requires approval)
    - Approved external collaboration

# Note: This rule requires auditing to be enabled for mailbox actions.

The rule was created from source IP 45.33.32.156, which was previously observed conducting an Nmap SYN scan. Immediate actions included session revocation, firewall blocking of the malicious IP, full endpoint scan (clean), and execution of an email client hardening playbook.

title: Suspicious Mailbox Forwarding Rule Creation
id: 8a9f3b4e-1c2d-4f5a-9b6c-7d8e9f0a1b2c
status: experimental
description: Detects creation of mailbox forwarding rules with sensitive keywords in enterprise email systems.
references:
    - https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/exchange/set-mailbox?view=exchange-ps
author: SOC Team
logsource:
    category: email
    product: exchange
    service: powershell
detection:
    selection:
        EventID: 1
        CmdletName: 'Set-Mailbox'
        Parameters:
            - Name: 'ForwardingSmtpAddress'
              Value: '*@*.com'
        Message: '*merger* OR *acquisition* OR *board* OR *confidential*'
    condition: selection
level: high

arguments.summary: Unauthorized mailbox forwarding rule was created on the executive assistant's account (exec.assistant@corp.local), resulting in the exfiltration of approximately 340 sensitive emails containing keywords such as 'merger', 'acquisition', 'board', and 'confidential'. The rule was established from external IP 45.33.32.156 and forwarded data to an external Gmail address. Immediate containment actions included password and MFA reset for the compromised user, blocking the malicious IP at the firewall, and scanning the host for malware, which returned no threats. No malicious payloads were found on the endpoint, and the source IP had prior scan activity but no direct lateral movement observed.

arguments.summary: A critical data exfiltration attempt was detected and blocked on production SQL server SRV-SQL-PROD-01. The service account 'svc-sql-prod' was misused to perform an unauthorized mysqldump of 4.2 million customer records. The dump file was staged in /tmp and an outbound SCP transfer to external IP 203.0.113.88 was initiated but blocked. Investigation revealed initial compromise via phishing (T1566.001) on workstation WS-FIN-042, leading to Cobalt Strike beacon deployment (T1071.001), lateral movement, and privilege escalation. The attacker attempted to use the service account for data staging and exfiltration. All sessions and credentials for the compromised service account have been revoked. A full host scan identified a secondary malicious binary on the SQL server.

Encoded PowerShell executed from Outlook, downloading Cobalt Strike beacon.
rundll32.exe loads unsigned beacon.dll from Temp directory.
Cobalt Strike beacon establishes C2 communication with 198.51.100.23.
Attacker performs lateral movement via SMB to file server.
Unauthorized mysqldump of customer_records database initiated by svc-sql-prod on SRV-SQL-PROD-01.
SCP exfiltration attempt to 203.0.113.88 detected and blocked by firewall.
Service account svc-sql-prod sessions and API keys revoked.
Full EPP scan of SRV-SQL-PROD-01 detects hidden malicious binary.

title: Unauthorized mysqldump by Service Account
logsource:
    product: linux
    service: auditd
    category: process_creation
    definition: 'Process creation events from auditd'
detection:
    selection:

}

arguments.summary: A critical data exfiltration attempt was detected and blocked on 2026-04-09 involving the unauthorized dumping of 4.2 million customer records from the 'customer_records' database. The attack originated from a compromised user account (CORP\jsmith) on endpoint WS-FIN-042, which deployed Cobalt Strike via phishing. Lateral movement was achieved to the production SQL server (SRV-SQL-PROD-01), where a service account (svc-sql-prod) was misused to initiate an SCP transfer of a compressed database dump to an external IP (203.0.113.88). The exfiltration was blocked by the firewall. All malicious artifacts were identified and contained.

timeline.description: Initial access: Outlook launched on WS-FIN-042 (CORP\jsmith).
Execution: Encoded PowerShell command executed from Outlook, dropping Cobalt Strike beacon.
Defense Evasion: Unsigned beacon.dll loaded via rundll32 from Temp directory.
Command & Control: Cobalt Strike beacon established to 198.51.100.23 (ET TROJAN alert triggered).
Lateral Movement: Successful SMB access from WS-FIN-042 to SRV-SQL-PROD-01.
Exfiltration: mysqldump executed by svc-sql-prod on SRV-SQL-PROD-01, staging 1.8GB dump file at /tmp/.cache/system_backup.sql.gz.
Exfiltration Attempt: SCP transfer initiated to external IP 203.0.113.88.
Containment: Firewall blocked outbound connection to 203.0.113.88; rule FW-RULE-0054 activated.
Credential Revocation: All sessions and API keys for svc-sql-prod revoked.
Malware Containment: Full scan detected and quarantined malicious file on SRV-SQL-PROD-01.

arguments.summary: A critical data exfiltration attempt was detected and thwarted on 2026-04-09. The service account 'svc-sql-prod' was compromised and used to execute an unauthorized mysqldump of the 'customer_records' database (4.2M rows) on SRV-SQL-PROD-01. The 1.8GB dump was staged in /tmp and an SCP exfiltration attempt to 203.0.113.88 was blocked by the firewall. Root cause traced to a phishing compromise of user 'jsmith' on WS-FIN-042, leading to Cobalt Strike beacon deployment, lateral movement, and privilege escalation to the service account. No data was exfiltrated, but the service account credentials were revoked and the database server hardened.

timeline.description: User CORP\jsmith opens phishing email in Outlook, launching malicious PowerShell.
PowerShell decodes and drops Cobalt Strike beacon (beacon.dll) in Temp directory.
rundll32.exe executes beacon.dll, establishing C2 beacon to 198.51.100.23.
IDS alerts on Cobalt Strike beacon traffic from WS-FIN-042.
Attacker performs lateral movement via SMB to database server SRV-SQL-PROD-01.
Unauthorized mysqldump executed by compromised 'svc-sql-prod' account on customer_records database.
SCP exfiltration attempt to 203.0.113.88 blocked by firewall rule.
Service account 'svc-sql-prod' sessions and API keys revoked.
Database server SRV-SQL-PROD-01 hardened via Ansible playbook.

arguments.rule_content:
title: Suspicious mysqldump by Service Account
logsource:
    product: linux
    service: auditd
    category: process_creation
    definition: 'Process starts with name mysqldump'
detection:
    selection:
        process_name: mysqldump
        user_name|re: 'svc-.*'
    condition: selection
level: high
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1003/
falsepositives:
    - Legitimate backup processes (mitigated by time/window check)
author: SOC Team

rule CobaltStrike_Beacon_DLL
{
    meta:
        description = "Detects common Cobalt Strike beacon DLL in memory or disk"
        author = "SOC Team"
        reference = "https://attack.mitre.org/software/S0154/"
        date = "2026-04-09"
    strings:
        $beacon_config = { 2E 2E 2F 63 6F 6E 66 69 67 2E 62 69 6E } // "../config.bin" pattern
        $http_get = "GET / HTTP/1.1" ascii
        $http_post = "POST / HTTP/1.1" ascii
        $user_agent = "Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 6.1; WOW64; Trident/7.0; rv:11.0) like Gecko" ascii
    condition:
        all of them
}
